newsitem.title: INDONESIA: California set on expanding trade with Asia.
newsitem.headline: California set on expanding trade with Asia.

text.p: California Governor Pete Wilson said on Wednesday his state was determined to be part of Asia's economic growth by strengthening its trade links with countries in the region, such as Indonesia.

"We are determined to be part of their economic growth," Wilson told an American Chamber of Commerce lunch in Jakarta. "I am convinced that the reality is that Asia will continue (to have) explosive economic growth."
Wilson, on a two-day trade promotion visit, said California's exports to Indonesia, which include produce and electronic goods, grew by almost 34 percent in 1995.
"In the first quarter of 1996, they grew by an additional 34.5 percent. This represents a full 15 percent of the total from all of the United States," he said without elaborating.

Wilson said California's exports to members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which groups Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, rose more than 36 percent in the first six months of 1996.

He said that in order to enhance economic cooperation with the Asian countries, California had opened trade offices in Hong Kong, Tokyo and Jakarta. Offices would be set up in Seoul and Shanghai soon, he added.
